answer: An agent economy can blunt Sybil attacks by tying every identity to a locked collateral bond that is slashed on proof of fraud. Picture a summit where only agents holding a jade credential may trade; that credential is issued once per verified deposit, so a cloned name needs a brand-new deposit of its own. A trellis of cross-checks then punishes any node that vouches for a twin, so each fake account costs a fresh bond plus the threat of losing it. Minting a thousand shells thus demands a thousand stakes, making identity farming a guaranteed loss.
